name: ntpd
description: ntpd(8) detaches, reads /etc/ntp.conf and stays up: ps lists a process named ntpd (the marker is built only then, since its log lines also carry the name), and its log shows it failing to resolve a named server.  /etc/rc starts it only when /etc/netstart brought the network up, and the harness has no network card, so the command starts it.  /etc/resolv.conf names a nameserver no route reaches, so each lookup really queries and the resolver's wait has to end on its own.  The staged ntp.conf also names 127.0.0.2, a peer that needs no lookup, and ntpdc(8) asks ntpd over lo0 for its peer table and prints that peer: ntpd answers nothing when it has no peers.
command: /sbin/ntpd; sleep 5; ps ax | grep 'ntp[d]$' > /tmp/p; test -s /tmp/p && echo NTPD''UP; sleep 10; ntpdc -n 127.0.0.1
